phase3_findings.description: Acceptance criterion 20 is unmet: the PR description is still the placeholder ('Work in progress — automated review pending. Resolves #375'). It does not name part 1a's changelog sentence 'Row rules are not supported yet' in changelog.d/389.added.md, and it does not say that the unreleased fragment needs a correction through the codex/changelog-notes-<reason> route.

docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md:99 says '_rewrite does not catch it', but two functions have that name: the module-level _rewrite (safety/rule_sets.py:583), which never calls guard_spec, and RuleSetGuardRunner._rewrite (:859), which does. The sentence also leaves out that run_sql's except Exception turns the error into a fail-closed refusal.
ReferencedByRule stores its two variants as three independent optional fields, and only the _variant validator enforces the exclusive-or, so callers coerce with 'or ""'.
CompareRule.value is typed Any; the scalar-or-list constraint is enforced only in _operand.

LoadedRuleSets.compiled is a public, mutable dict that defaults to empty, and the rule that every row rule has a compiled rule is checked only in guard_spec (which fails closed). GuardSpec.tables is a plain dict next to the MappingProxyType-wrapped rules.

## Verdict: REJECT (one Important finding at the threshold: acceptance criterion 20 is unmet)
The code is ready, but the PR is not ready to merge: its description is still the placeholder text and does not include the changelog correction note that criterion 20 requires.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major
1. The PR description does not meet acceptance criterion 20. The body reads only "Work in progress — automated review pending. Resolves #375". It does not name part 1a's changelog sentence "Row rules are not supported yet" in `changelog.d/389.added.md`, and it does not say that, while that fragment is unreleased, it needs a correction through the release guide's `codex/changelog-notes-<reason>` route. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: the PR description is prose that no tool reads for behavior; changing it changes no output; it is published to readers outside the repository, so it is capped at Important -->

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)
<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md:99` says "`_rewrite` does not catch it". The name is ambiguous: `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` defines a module-level `_rewrite` (line 583), which never calls `guard_spec`, and the method `RuleSetGuardRunner._rewrite` (line 859), which does. The sentence also leaves out that `run_sql`'s broad `except Exception` turns the error into a fail-closed refusal. (raised by 1/6 agents; the code reviewer noted the same sentence below its reporting bar)
2. In `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:271-292`, `ReferencedByRule` stores its two variants as three independent optional fields, and only the `_variant` validator enforces the exclusive-or. As a result, callers coerce with `node.source_column or ""` (lines 395, 397, 610, 619). (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `CompareRule.value` in `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:204` is typed `Any`. The scalar-or-list constraint is enforced only in `_operand`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. In `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:670-699`, `LoadedRuleSets.compiled` is a public, mutable dict that defaults to empty. The rule that every row rule has a compiled rule is checked only in `guard_spec`, which raises `RuntimeError` and fails closed. Also, `GuardSpec.tables` is a plain dict next to the `MappingProxyType`-wrapped `rules`. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

- VC-67: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — Under the example set, on a server with MySQL's default `optimizer_switch`, MySQL's `EXPLAIN` of the SQL the guard produces for `SELECT c.name, o.total, cu.code FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN currencies cu ON cu.id = 1` shows the derived tables for `customers` and `orders` as materialized (`select_type` `DERIVED`) and no materialized derived table for `currencies`. So each reference to a table with a row rule is built in full, with every row its rule leaves visible, before the model's own conditions apply, and that work counts against the statement timeout; a table without a row rule stays mergeable. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Criterion 10 counts (criteria.json is a valid list). Code read: src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py _rewrite (583-604) wraps a table with a row rule via _scoped_body (405-422), which ends in LIMIT 18446744073709551615 (_MATERIALIZE_LIMIT, 182); a table without a rule goes through _derived (322-332), a plain SELECT cols FROM t with no LIMIT/WHERE. That is the construction the claim relies on, and MySQL's documented rule that a derived table with LIMIT cannot be merged is consistent with it. But the claim is about the output of MySQL EXPLAIN (select_type DERIVED rows, and currencies not DERIVED) on a default-optimizer_switch server, which reading cannot settle. tests/connectors/test_row_rules_mysql.py:295-315 asserts exactly this, but I did not run it (no MySQL server run: pytest tests/connectors/test_row_rules_mysql.py::test_explain_shows_scoped_tables_materialized_and_unscoped_mergeable).
